title: One affine section chart at the strict-local identity
statement: Let $A$ be a normal Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $k$ be its residue field [def-weil-residue-field], choose a separable closure $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and let $R=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the strict henselization with that residue-field embedding [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]. Let $p:H\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e$, and with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $(B,r,\tau)$ be a cubical rigidified invertible module on $H$ [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line, def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that for EVERY prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the pullback $B_{\mathfrak p}$ to $H\times_A\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is ample [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Put $X=H\times_A\operatorname{Spec}R$, $L=B|_X$, and let $e_R$ be its identity section. There exist an integer $n\geq1$ and a global section $s\in\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes n})$ such that the nonvanishing open $X_s$ is affine and $s(e_R(\mathfrak m_R))\ne0$ at the closed identity. This asserts existence of a single affine nonvanishing chart, not a covering of $X$.

source.place: Agent-formulated strict-local affine-chart input for the fibrewise cubical ampleness argument. Raynaud original unavailable locally; no numbered assertion of that source is claimed. All residue-fibre ampleness assumptions are retained.

proof.text: We use the following elementary section arguments, on any quasi-compact scheme $Z$. If $E$ is ample and $V$ is globally generated, choose at $z$ a section $t$ of $E^a$ with affine $Z_t$ and a section $v$ of $V$ nonzero at $z$. Then $t\otimes v^a$ is a section of $(E\otimes V)^a$, nonzero at $z$; its locus is $Z_t\cap Z_v$, affine by the affine-cap lemma. Hence $E\otimes V$ is ample. If $E,F$ are both ample, a positive power $F^b$ is globally generated by the coherent-twist theorem applied to $\mathcal O_Z$; $E^b$ is ample by the positive-power theorem. The preceding argument makes $(E\otimes F)^b$ ample. An ample positive power implies the line itself ample directly from the definition, by interpreting sections of $(L^b)^a$ as sections of $L^{ab}$. We use these section arguments below, including their last positive-power converse.

source.place: Agent assembly from the separately cited generic torus quotient, endomorphism span, generic-line comparison and norm-reflection inputs; original source WANTED.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $\eta$ be its generic point. Normality of the local ring makes $A$ an integrally closed domain, so $S$ is normal integral Noetherian affine. Semiabelian geometric fibres are connected and nonempty: a clopen decomposition is constant on every coset of the connected split torus, descends through its fppf quotient to the connected abelian variety, and is constant; the identity gives nonemptiness. Apply the generic torus-quotient theorem to get $q:H\to J$, a torsor under a torus $T/S$, with $J/S$ smooth separated commutative of finite presentation, semiabelian fibres, and $J_\eta$ an abelian variety. The normal-smooth-group local-ample theorem gives ample lines on $J$ over an affine open cover of $S$. Any member containing the closed point of the local scheme $S$ is all of $S$, so obtain an ample line $M$ on $J$. Put $F=M\otimes[-1]^*M$. Inversion is an affine isomorphism, so its pullback of $M$ is ample; step 1 makes $F$ ample, and tensor symmetry makes it symmetric.

source.place: Agent assembly from the separately cited generic torus quotient, endomorphism span, generic-line comparison and norm-reflection inputs; original source WANTED.

proof.text: The torus $T/S$ is affine: fppf locally it is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$, hence affine, and affineness descends along fpqc coverings. Likewise $q$ is affine: it is an fpqc cover, and its base change along itself is the projection $H\times_ST\to H$ by the torsor identity, which is affine by base change from $T\to S$. Apply affine fpqc descent to $q$. Consequently $q^*$ preserves ampleness by the ample affine-pullback theorem. The morphisms $J_\eta\to J$ and $H_\eta\to H$ are affine too, since they are base changes of the morphism between affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)\to S$. In particular $F_\eta$ is symmetric ample.

source.place: Agent assembly from the separately cited generic torus quotient, endomorphism span, generic-line comparison and norm-reflection inputs; original source WANTED.

proof.text: Write $N=B\otimes\iota^*B$. The assumed ampleness of $B_{(0)}=B_\eta$, inversion and step 1 make $N_\eta$ ample. Apply rational Picard surjectivity for the torus torsor $q_\eta:H_\eta\to J_\eta$ to $B_\eta$. Its target is smooth, separated and finite type; it is geometrically integral by the smooth-connected-fibre integrality theorem, since its geometric fibres are semiabelian and hence connected as checked in step 2. Obtain $c\ge1$ and a line $D$ on $J_\eta$ with $q_\eta^*D\simeq B_\eta^c$. Set $C=D\otimes[-1]^*D$. This line is symmetric and, since $q$ commutes with inversion, $q_\eta^*C\simeq N_\eta^c$, which is ample. Apply the separate abelian-quotient ample-reflection theorem to this semiabelian extension to deduce that $C$ itself is ample on $J_\eta$. This reflection is specific to an extension of an abelian variety by a torus, not a general fpqc descent of absolute ampleness.

source.place: Agent assembly from the separately cited generic torus quotient, endomorphism span, generic-line comparison and norm-reflection inputs; original source WANTED.

proof.text: Apply coherent-twist global generation on $J_\eta$ with ample line $C$ and the finite-type quasi-coherent line $F_\eta^{-1}$. Choose $d\ge2$ so that $F_\eta^{-1}\otimes C^{d-1}$ is globally generated. By step 1, $E=C^d\otimes F_\eta^{-1}$ is ample, and it is symmetric. Apply the symmetric-ample endomorphism-span theorem to $F_\eta$ and $E$ on the abelian variety $J_\eta$. It gives $a\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and endomorphisms $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ with $E^a\simeq\bigotimes b_j^*F_\eta$. Extend each $b_j$ uniquely to an endomorphism of $J/S$ by normal-semiabelian generic homomorphism extension. Define the actual line $Q=F^a\otimes\bigotimes b_j^*F$ on all of $J$. The displayed comparison gives $Q_\eta\simeq F_\eta^a\otimes E^a\simeq C^{da}$.

source.place: Agent assembly from the separately cited generic torus quotient, endomorphism span, generic-line comparison and norm-reflection inputs; original source WANTED.

proof.text: Choose $v\ge1$ so that $F^v$ is generated by finitely many global sections, again by coherent-twist global generation with $\mathcal O_J$. Their pullbacks generate every $b_j^*F^v$: at a point a nonzero generating fibre value pulls back to a nonzero value after the residue-field extension, by the invertible-pullback fibre formula. The tensor-globally-generated theorem makes $V=\bigotimes b_j^*F^v$ globally generated (and supplies finite generators); $J$ is quasi-compact, as a finitely presented scheme over affine $S$. The line $F^{av}$ is ample by the positive-power theorem. Step 1 therefore makes $Q^v=F^{av}\otimes V$ ample and then makes $Q$ ample. Hence $q^*Q$ is ample on $H$ by step 3.

source.place: Agent assembly from the separately cited generic torus quotient, endomorphism span, generic-line comparison and norm-reflection inputs; original source WANTED.

proof.text: With $h=cda>0$, step 4 and step 5 give $(q^*Q)_\eta\simeq N_\eta^h$. Thus $V=N^h\otimes(q^*Q)^{-1}$ is generically trivial. Apply the normal-Noetherian generic-line-pullback theorem to $p:H\to S$ and $V$. Both schemes are locally Noetherian: $S$ is Noetherian and $H$ is finite type over $S$. Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation. All residue fibres are integral and nonempty by the smooth-connected-fibre normal-integrality theorem, using the connectedness checked in step 2. Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness, so its last hypothesis holds as well. Obtain $V\simeq p^*W$ for an invertible module $W$ on $S$. This module is trivial: a trivializing open containing the closed point of $S$ is all of $S$. Consequently $N^h\simeq q^*Q$ is ample. The positive-power converse in step 1 gives that the supplied global norm $N$ is ample on $H$.

source.place: Agent assembly from the separately cited generic torus quotient, endomorphism span, generic-line comparison and norm-reflection inputs; original source WANTED.

proof.text: Apply cubical ample-norm reflection over $S$ to the GIVEN $(B,r,\tau)$. Its base is normal integral Noetherian affine and its group is smooth separated commutative of finite presentation with semiabelian geometric fibres, as required. Step 7 verifies its crucial hypothesis, absolute ampleness of $B\otimes\iota^*B$ on all of $H$, rather than only fibrewise ampleness. Its conclusion makes $B$ ample on $H$. No use is made of the parent fibrewise-ample criterion, the supplied-norm-ampleness theorem, or their descendants: those would be circular here.

proof.text: The projection $g:X=H\times_A\operatorname{Spec}R\to H$ is affine, being the base change of a morphism between affine schemes. Pullback of the ample $B$ along $g$ makes $L$ ample on $X$. Apply the definition of ampleness at the point $e_R(\mathfrak m_R)$. It supplies $n\ge1$ and $s\in\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes n})$ with affine $X_s$ containing that point. Membership in the nonvanishing locus means exactly $s(e_R(\mathfrak m_R))\ne0$, as required. All residue-fibre hypotheses of the original statement are retained; the argument uses in particular the generic one.
